title: Private Pilot - Access Paths & Telemetry Sync
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on access paths into Redwood Private (VPC peering vs. private link vs. transit), telemetry mapping, and plan/risks for kernel v1.3 rollout. Agreed to run a controlled latency soak and deliver detailed telemetry mapping. Security team raised SOC2 and KMS logging questions; Redwood to supply audit log examples and SAML metadata.
topics: network access options (peering, private link, transit)
action_items: Daniel Sosa: run 1-hour latency soak on staging with kernel v1.3 and default batching (due 2025-06-27)
Liam O'Connor: produce telemetry mapping sheet tying Redwood Console metrics to VeraHealth dashboards (due 2025-06-26)
Maya Chen: share SOC2 audit-log extract and SAML metadata for demo (due 2025-06-26)
Alina Park: confirm KMS provider and key rotation window (due 2025-06-30)
next_steps: Staging soak and telemetry export by end of week
Follow-up security deep-dive scheduled for 2025-07-01 10:00 PST
Canary cutover target 2025-07-02 pending soak results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Priya (CTO, VeraHealth), Daniel (NetOps), Alina (SecOps), Marco (SRE)

Summary/Notes (auto): quick status, telemetry, kernel upgrade triage, access path decision.

00:00:01 Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, quick agenda: access paths, telemetry mapping, kernel v1.3 rollout, risks and any blockers.
00:00:08 Priya Nair: thanks Maya, yep we wanna prioritize minimal blast radius, like ideally we keep production on current kernel until we validate.
00:00:15 Liam O'Connor: absolutely, what we saw in the lab was a 3–6ms median uplift on some short sequences when quant path hit a fallback kernel, not consistent but noticeable.
00:00:30 Marco Ten: right, and in our last run we saw a few 200ms spikes at tail, which correlated to egress retries. unsure if it's TCP MTU or sidecar retransmits.
00:00:43 Daniel Sosa: we suspect MTU mismatch between customer sidecar and the transit gateway — we have jumbo frames on our infra but not sure the pilot VPC path honors it.
00:00:55 Liam O'Connor: okay that's helpful, one thing to call out is the private link vs peering difference: peering preserves MTU more directly but requires route table maintenance; private link uses a managed endpoint and sometimes imposes MTU 1500.
00:01:12 Priya Nair: so you're saying peering might reduce those retransmits?
00:01:16 Liam O'Connor: it can, yes, especially if you avoid an extra NAT hop. But peering means you manage the route filters; private link gives an easier operational model and SLA.
00:01:27 Alina Park: security-wise private link is nicer because we get fewer public-exposed egress points, but we need to see audit logs for inbound connections and key access patterns. do you have log samples?
00:01:39 Maya Chen: we do, we'll share SOC2-friendly extracts. Liam we'll attach a redacted audit-log example.
00:01:45 Liam O'Connor: noted, I'll pull the extract and also include SAML metadata and instructions for SSO.
00:02:02 Sofia Ruiz: for timeline, if we see acceptable results from the soak, we can schedule a canary early next week, otherwise postpone.
00:02:10 Priya Nair: yes, important to get the telemetry mapping done first so our observability team can correlate.
00:02:18 Liam O'Connor: on telemetry, Redwood Console exposes token-level latency, model-level qps, kv cache hit ratio, batching stats, and per-request routing reasons. We’ll map those to your dashboards.
00:02:31 Daniel Sosa: can you export that via prometheus or a push gateway? we run Grafana/Prometheus internally.
00:02:37 Liam O'Connor: currently we have an export endpoint that pushes Prometheus metrics and a JSON API for detailed traces. We'll provide a mapping sheet with metric names and units.
00:02:46 Marco Ten: perfect. also would like the trace id propagate into our sidecar so we can stitch request across our infra.
00:02:52 Liam O'Connor: yes trace-id header is supported, we documented X-Redwood-Trace and will include examples.
00:03:03 Priya Nair: switching to kernel v1.3, can you recap what's changed and why we saw variability?
00:03:10 Liam O'Connor: sure, v1.3 includes a new attention kernel optimized for long-context batching and a fallback for some quantized ops. The optimization helps throughput for long sequences but, in edge cases, the fallback path can cause per-token variance. We suspect that a small interaction with our OS network stack and burst batching timing is amplifying latency tail.
00:03:34 Marco Ten: are you able to force older kernel if we hit issues?
00:03:37 Liam O'Connor: yes you can pin runtime to v1.2 for the route — that's how we plan canary. Also we have automatic rollback if 95th% latency exceeds threshold.
00:03:48 Priya Nair: what's the rollback detection interval?
00:03:51 Maya Chen: currently set to 5 minutes on the canary policy but we can shorten for pilot to 1 minute.
00:03:58 Daniel Sosa: shorter is safer for us.
00:04:02 Priya Nair: the big question: for production cutover we need an audit trail, KMS key separation, and evidence that route failover works without data leakage.
00:04:12 Alina Park: on KMS, we use AWS KMS with CMKs; will Redwood integrate with our key aliasing and rotate?
00:04:20 Liam O'Connor: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS via a key-access proxy. We don't hold your plaintext; we call your KMS and store references. We can show logs for key calls.
00:04:30 Alina Park: we'll need a sample showing the key call-and-audit entries.
00:04:35 Maya Chen: action, we'll send redacted examples.
00:04:41 Priya Nair: any competitor risk if we go with Redwood? our procurement asked if Anthropic or OpenAI options would be easier.
00:04:47 Maya Chen: those are options but Anthropic/OpenAI would be hosted public endpoints; you lose the private deployment control and the route-level rollback we provide. Also cost profiles differ.
00:04:59 Daniel Sosa: procurement also asked about egress costs and bandwidth budgeting. Do you have a calculator?
00:05:05 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a model showing tokens x throughput x egress, and Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching to reduce cost.
00:05:13 Sofia Ruiz: back to telemetry, Liam can you walk briefly through the mapping plan?
00:05:18 Liam O'Connor: sure — high level: 1) baseline metrics we export: request_latency_ms, request_qps, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kernel_version, route_reason. 2) traces include step durations: preprocesing, tokenization, model_execution, postprocess. 3) we will produce a CSV mapping with labels you already use in Grafana and example PromQLs.
00:05:39 Marco Ten: will that include the edge router health? we need per-hop latency.
00:05:43 Liam O'Connor: per-hop is there when using our telemetry proxy; if you're on peering we can add the transit gateway hops. There's some sampling though, full packet-level tracing isn't feasible but you get per-request hop timings.
00:05:57 Daniel Sosa: good enough. for the soak, what's the exact config we should run?
00:06:03 Maya Chen: propose: kernel v1.3, default batching, KV cache enabled with TTL 300s, run 1 hour at representative QPS (we suggest 60% of peak), collect Prometheus scrape and full traces for 5% of requests.
00:06:18 Daniel Sosa: ok we'll schedule that late Friday night to avoid impact.
00:06:23 Priya Nair: also confirm that fallback to v1.2 will not leak model keys or requests to hosted pool. I've seen docs about automatic fallback to compatible variants — need clarity.
00:06:35 Liam O'Connor: good call. fallback is to another private runtime in your reserved pool; we don't route to public hosted unless you configure hybrid fallback. For the pilot we'll keep fallback restricted to your Dedicated/Private pool.
00:06:50 Alina Park: verification: so in case of capacity shortfall, it won't spill to Redwood hosted?
00:06:54 Maya Chen: not in the pilot defaults, no spillover. We'll show policy JSON for route config.
00:07:03 Priya Nair: security deep dive — we need to understand RBAC granularity for operators, and audit log retention and export.
00:07:11 Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports RBAC with roles: admin/operator/viewer and you can map to SAML groups. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or forwarded to an event collector for retention control.
00:07:23 Alina Park: acceptable if you can show an example.
00:07:27 Liam O'Connor: will include sample S3 object structure for audit logs.
00:07:33 Sofia Ruiz: quick check: any blockers on dependencies?
00:07:36 Marco Ten: we need the SAML metadata and the KMS integration to be validated before canary, so those are gating.
00:07:43 Maya Chen: understood, we'll push SAML metadata and audit logs by tomorrow.
00:07:49 Daniel Sosa: also want to call out NAT timeouts — we saw TCP connections being closed after 350s causing mid-stream reconnects.
00:07:58 Liam O'Connor: thanks, we'll include recommended NAT timeout settings in the runbook.
00:08:04 Priya Nair: any rough numbers on expected 95th% latency for the canary?
00:08:09 Liam O'Connor: based on lab runs at 60% QPS, we expect p95 to be within 20–40ms of your current baseline if KV cache is warmed; tail spikes were the issue we want to soak.
00:08:20 Marco Ten: acceptable as long as we can abort quickly.
00:08:24 Maya Chen: we'll set the canary to 1-minute detection and auto-rollback on p95 delta > 30ms.
00:08:32 Daniel Sosa: for rollout plan, can we do split traffic 5%/95% then 25/75 then 50/50?
00:08:38 Liam O'Connor: yes our rollout supports progressive increments and pause on anomaly.
00:08:44 Priya Nair: okay good.
00:08:47 Sofia Ruiz: we're getting good alignment. Let's dig into the telemetry details — Liam, do you have the metric names on hand?
00:08:54 Liam O'Connor: yes here: redwood_request_latency_ms (gauge histogram), redwood_request_count_total, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kernel_version{ver}, redwood_route_decision{reason}. For traces: we annotate trace span: tokenization, model_exec, kv_lookup.
00:09:12 Daniel Sosa: will we be able to tag requests with our tenant-id header so we can apply per-tenant dashboards?
00:09:18 Liam O'Connor: yes header X-Tenant-ID or we can do per-route scoping. We'll show examples.
00:09:24 Priya Nair: moving to risks: what are the top 3 residual risks for the canary?
00:09:29 Liam O'Connor: 1) tail latency due to fallback timing; 2) MTU/middlebox causing retransmits; 3) missing telemetry mapping causing delayed detection.
00:09:39 Marco Ten: add NAT timeouts as #4.
00:09:42 Maya Chen: action — we'll mitigate 1 by short detection window and pin fallback to private pool, 2 by recommending peering or verifying MTU, 3 by delivering the mapping sheet prior to canary, 4 by recommended NAT settings plus keepalive.
00:09:55 Priya Nair: good. Any open questions from security?
00:09:58 Alina Park: if you support HSM-backed KMS, can we see the key access frequency?
00:10:03 Liam O'Connor: yes we surface key call metrics and can show them in the mapping sheet.
00:10:09 Daniel Sosa: quick clarification, is the Prometheus endpoint pull or push?
00:10:12 Liam O'Connor: we support pull if you can reach the endpoint, otherwise a pushgateway option exists.
00:10:19 Marco Ten: which do you recommend for private link?
00:10:22 Liam O'Connor: private link tends to favor push since the endpoint is behind the managed interface; peering often allows direct pull.
00:10:30 Priya Nair: good to note.
00:10:33 Sofia Ruiz: we should capture the decision: peering for performance if VeraHealth can manage routes; private link for simplified ops and better procurement alignment.
00:10:43 Priya Nair: we'll choose peering for staging soak to minimize MTU issues, then evaluate private link for long-term.
00:10:50 Maya Chen: noted.
00:10:55 Liam O'Connor: quick note on observability retention: Redwood Console keeps traces 7 days by default in pilot; you can increase retention for an add-on.
00:11:03 Priya Nair: procurement will want that documented.
00:11:07 Maya Chen: we'll include retention options in the follow-up docs.
00:11:10 Daniel Sosa: any final items before we list actions?
00:11:14 Priya Nair: just set the canary rollback to 1 minute and ensure no cross-tenant fallthrough.
00:11:19 Maya Chen: got it. Recap of action items: Daniel run soak, Liam telemetry sheet + audit logs, Maya SOC2 examples + policy JSON, Alina confirm KMS. We'll sync again after soak.
00:11:33 Sofia Ruiz: scheduling note — security deep dive on 2025-07-01 10:00 PST.
00:11:38 Priya Nair: confirmed.
00:11:41 Maya Chen: great thanks everyone.
00:11:43 (meeting wraps; informal chatter)

Transcript quality notes: speaker attribution mostly correct, occasional mis-heard terms (quant path spelled as quantized 'quant' etc.). Some timestamps approximate.

Detailed transcript (continued, excerpts):
00:12:12 Daniel Sosa: starting soak now in staging, kernel 1.3 flagged. we'll collect prometheus and full traces for sampled 5%. plan to run 60 minutes.
00:12:26 Liam O'Connor: thanks Daniel, please also leave KV cache cold for first 10 minutes then warm to observe cold-start behavior.
00:12:35 Marco Ten: will do, we can schedule a warm-up and then the real run.
00:12:41 Priya Nair: do you have a test harness for sequence length distribution matching our prod?
00:12:46 Liam O'Connor: we do; send sample logs and we can generate a synthetic workload that mirrors your token distribution.
00:12:54 Priya Nair: we'll export a day of anonymized traffic.
00:12:58 Maya Chen: perfect.
00:13:05 Alina Park: on the SAML side, what's the expected attribute mapping?
00:13:09 Liam O'Connor: email, groups, nameid. We'll provide a sample metadata and attribute map.
00:13:15 Alina Park: ok.
00:13:18 Daniel Sosa: starting soak now — logging out.
00:13:22 (call participants leave in small groups)

End of recording.

Post-call notes (auto): The group agreed to do a staging soak with kernel v1.3 and follow up with security deep-dive. Redwood to deliver mapping sheet, audit-log examples and policy JSON. Customer to validate KMS details and NAT timeouts.
